lines.text: Practice — Reason and Investigate
PRACTICE
Raman says: "All starches are carbohydrates, but not all carbohydrates are
starches." Is he right?
Design an activity that would test his claim, stating what you would use,
what you would do, and what result would support him.
You are handed an unlabelled solution and told it may be iodine solution.
Describe how you would find out, using only what is in your kitchen.
State what result would confirm it and what result would rule it out.
Millets grow on less water and carry more fibre and minerals than polished rice.
Yet polished rice replaced millets across much of urban India.
Suggest two reasons why a food that is worse on nutrition might still win.
(Consider cost, cooking time, storage, and what people believe about food.)
Lind's 1746 comparison of two groups of sailors is described on page 11.
Why was it stronger evidence than one doctor's opinion about lemons?
What would have made it stronger still?
BEYOND
Beyond the Book
e Read three labels. Next time groceries are unpacked at home, find three
packaged items and copy their nutrition panels. Rank them from best to
worst as an everyday food and write two lines defending your ranking.
Salt without a factory. The Apatani people of Arunachal Pradesh traditionally
make a salt called tapyo from plant ash rather than from seawater or rock.
Find out how, and why a community would develop such a method.
Write a short account with pictures.
Wild food near you. In many parts of India people gather uncultivated
greens, fruit and mushrooms — the ranbhajis of Maharashtra are one
example. find out whether anything is gathered wild near your town.
Ask an older person; they will know things the internet does not.
• Write to your principal. Wth your classmates, list the junk foods most
often eaten in your school. Then write a joint letter to your principal
proposing which to remove from the canteen and what to offer instead.
Cost your alternatives — a proposal nobody can afford will be refused.
